description: Polish Romantic composer, the central figure of the lyrical piano. His music is idiomatically pianistic: a singing, heavily ornamented right-hand cantilena floating over a wide-spread, pedal-sustained left-hand accompaniment.
harmonic_language: Chromatic voice leading, frequent secondary dominants and diminished-seventh chords, expressive modulations to remote keys, Neapolitan and augmented-sixth chords at cadences, suspensions and appoggiaturas for tension.
style_notes: Right-hand melody is a vocal, legato line with rubato; decorate it with turns, trills, grace notes, and rapid filigree runs (cadenza-like flourishes), especially in repeats and reprises.
Left hand: wide broken-chord / arpeggiated accompaniment spanning more than an octave (bass note on beat 1, then the chord spread above), rhythmically steady to contrast the free melody.
Phrases are mostly 4 + 4 bars (antecedent / consequent) with clear arch contours and breathing rests between phrases.
Rich use of the sustain pedal implies overlapping harmonies; keep the bass note ringing under the figuration.
Dynamics are nuanced: frequent hairpins, sudden p subito, climaxes approached by chromatic ascent.
Favor a 6/8 or 3/4 lilt in nocturnes and waltzes; dotted rhythms and triplet subdivisions are common.
